# 2.0.0: API cleanup, the announced removals, and three feature gaps

## Purpose

The core split shipped as `2.0.0-preview.2`: three packages, new namespaces, new repository name. Nothing about the *shape* of the API changed in it, and that was deliberate — the split plan called the renames "a separate workstream that lands in the same major after this plan". This document is that workstream, plus the three feature gaps that the 2026-09-04 reference-library evaluation identified as worth closing before the major closes.

It fixes WHAT changes, in WHICH order, and WHY. HOW each piece is verified follows the mandatory test-first workflow. When the plan completes, its durable content graduates into [specs/qrcode-symbologies.md](../specs/qrcode-symbologies.md) and the per-symbology records, and this file is deleted.

**The window argument.** A public API is added in a minor and removed only in a major. 2.0.0 is the only release in which the accumulated naming drift, the value-type inconsistencies and the deprecated overloads can all be corrected at once, and consumers are already editing every `using` line for the namespace change. Two edits in one line of caller code (`ECCLevel` → `QREccLevel` next to `CreateQrCode` → `Create`) cost the same as one. Everything in Phases 1-3 exists because of that arithmetic; after 2.0.0 the next chance is 3.0.0.

## Scope

| In | Out |
|---|---|
| The announced removals (`Compression`, `GetRequiredBufferSize` ×2, parameter-list generator overloads) | `CancellationToken` / time-budget decode overloads (additive, 2.1.0) |
| Type and method renames under one naming rule | Payload helpers (deferred by the maintainer; unchanged) |
| Value-kind, immutability and sealing unification | GS1 / FNC1 (unchanged) |
| Symbol geometry in the decode result | A pure-BCL SVG / 1-bit PNG writer (waits for a concrete request) |
| Structured Append, encode and decode (Standard QR only) | `EciMode` as a value type — decided against, see D7 |
| Kanji encoding for all three symbologies | Additional renderer packages |
| Migration table and a mechanical replacement script | Readability heuristics for styled output |

Features are additive and could ship in 2.1.0 without breaking anyone. They are in 2.0.0 because the maintainer chose to make the major a feature-complete line rather than a rename-only one. Kanji encoding is the largest and last of them precisely so it can be demoted to 2.1.0 without disturbing anything else if it slips.

## The naming rule

One rule decides every name in both packages:

> **A prefix says which symbology. No prefix means all three.** The prefixes are `QR` (Standard QR), `MicroQR` and `RmQR`. A noun that literally denotes *a code* keeps the `{Sym}Code` form (`QRCodeData`, `MicroQRCodeGenerator`, `RmQRCodeDecodeInfo`); everything else — enums, ranges, strategies — takes the short prefix. Three-letter acronyms are Pascal-cased (`Ecc`, `Eci`, `Bom`), which the existing `EccLevel` *properties* already are.

Micro QR and rMQR were built after the rule was implicit and already follow it. Every violation is in Standard QR, which was written first, or in a shared type that took the `QRCode` prefix while meaning "the family". That double meaning of `QRCode` — Standard QR in `QRCodeData`, the family in `QRCodeDecodeStatus` — is the actual defect the rule removes.

### Core (`FeatherQR`)

| Now | 2.0.0 | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `ECCLevel` | `QREccLevel` | The only unprefixed enum; siblings are `MicroQREccLevel` and `RmQREccLevel` |
| `QRCodeSegmentation` | `QRSegmentation` | Siblings are `MicroQRSegmentation`, `RmQRSegmentation` |
| `QRCodeVersionRange` | `QRVersionRange` | Sibling is `MicroQRVersionRange` |
| `QRCodeDecodeStatus` | `DecodeStatus` | Shared by all three symbologies; moves out of `QRCodeDecodeInfo.cs` into its own file |
| `QRCodeGenerator.CreateQrCode` | `QRCodeGenerator.Create` | The class already names the symbology; deletes the `Qr` / `QR` casing question rather than answering it |
| `MicroQRCodeGenerator.CreateMicroQRCode` | `MicroQRCodeGenerator.Create` | Same |
| `RmQRCodeGenerator.CreateRmQRCode` | `RmQRCodeGenerator.Create` | Same |
| `QRCodeCalculatedSize.QrSize`, `MicroQRCodeCalculatedSize.QrSize` | `Size` | Matches `QRCodeData.Size`; rMQR's `Width`/`Height` stay |
| `QRCodeGeneratorOptions.Utf8BOM` | `Utf8Bom` | Acronym rule |
| `Internals.StandardQr`, `Internals.RmQr` (namespaces) | `Internals.StandardQR`, `Internals.RmQR` | Internal, but the same rule. The `Internals/RmQr` folder is renamed with the namespace, so folder and namespace agree the way `MicroQR` and `StandardQR` already did |

### Rendering (`FeatherQR.SkiaSharp`)

| Now | 2.0.0 | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `QRCodeExtensions` | `SKCanvasExtensions` | It holds `SKCanvas` extension methods and nothing else; named after what it extends, as the BCL does |
| `QRCodeRenderer` | `SymbolRenderer` | Renders all three symbologies, so it takes no prefix; "symbol" is the word both standards use |
| `QRCodeImageBuilderBase<TSelf>` | `SymbolImageBuilderBase<TSelf>` | Same reasoning, same word |
| `Vector2Slim` (public) | internal | Appears in no public signature; it is an implementation detail that leaked into the surface |

### Names that deliberately do not change

`QRCodeData`, `QRCodeGenerator`, `QRCodeDecoder`, `QRCodeGeneratorOptions`, `QRCodeCalculatedSize`, `QRCodeDecodeInfo`, `QRCodeImageBuilder`, `QRCodeImageDecoder` and their Micro/rMQR siblings are all "a code" nouns and keep their form. `EciMode`, `ModuleRect` and the shape classes are already correct.

## Removals

| Removed | Announced in | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `Compression` | 1.2.0 `[Obsolete]` | No API accepts or returns it |
| `QRCodeGenerator.GetRequiredBufferSize`, `MicroQRCodeGenerator.GetRequiredBufferSize` | 1.2.0 `[Obsolete]` | `TryGetRequiredBufferSize` is the whole sizing surface afterwards |
| Parameter-list `CreateQrCode` / `CreateMicroQRCode` overloads | Spec, "frozen, removed at 2.0.0" | rMQR never had them and is the shape the other two converge on |
| `QRCodeCalculatedSize` public constructor and `IsValid` | Not previously announced | Part of the value-kind unification below, not of the removals phase; `IsValid` duplicates the `bool` that `TryGetRequiredBufferSize` already returns |

`IconData()` is **not** on this list, though the approved API listing shows it as `[Obsolete]`. The type has a `required` member, and that marker is what the compiler emits on the implicit constructor to stop a pre-C#-11 consumer from bypassing the required-member check.

Two consequences to handle inside the phase rather than discover later:

- **`SizingExceptionContractTest` disappears with its subject.** It pins the frozen disagreement between the two deprecated sizing methods (`InvalidOperationException` vs `ArgumentException` for overflow, `ArgumentException` vs `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` for an undefined ECC level). Once both throwing methods are gone the disagreement is gone; the spec paragraph describing it becomes a "lessons learned" entry rather than a live contract.
- **The `options` parameter can finally be defaulted everywhere.** The asymmetry the spec records ("rMQR defaults it, the other two cannot, because their parameter-list overloads would make the call ambiguous") is caused entirely by the overloads being removed here. After the removal all three generators read `Create(text, ecc, in {Sym}CodeGeneratorOptions options = default)`, which is the shape the spec wanted and could not have.

## Shape unification

| Item | Now | 2.0.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `*CalculatedSize` | QR is a `record struct` with a public constructor, `init` setters and `IsValid`; Micro/rMQR are plain `readonly struct`s with internal constructors | One kind: `readonly struct`, internal constructor, get-only properties, no `IsValid`. It is an `out` parameter of a `Try` method, never something a caller builds |
| `*DecodeInfo` | Three `readonly struct`s with different member order; rMQR has no `MaskPattern` (correct — rMQR has one fixed mask) | Same member order everywhere: `Status`, `Version`, `EccLevel`, `MaskPattern` where the symbology defines one, `ErrorsCorrected`, then the new geometry and Structured Append members |
| `GradientOptions` | `record class` holding `SKColor[]` and `float[]` through `init` properties, with a mutable `public static readonly Default` | `sealed class`, constructor copies both arrays, exposes them as read-only, structural equality over elements |
| `IconData` | `class` with public get/set properties and an `[Obsolete]` parameterless constructor | `sealed`, init-only properties, factory methods only |
| `QRCodeData`, `MicroQRCodeData`, `RmQRCodeData`, the three image builders | Non-sealed with no extension point | `sealed`. `SymbolImageBuilderBase<TSelf>` stays public and abstract with a `private protected` constructor; the shape classes stay open on purpose |

**`GradientOptions` carries a live defect, not just a shape problem.** A `record class` generates equality that compares `SKColor[]` by reference, so two gradients with identical colours already compare unequal, and `GradientOptions.Default.Colors[0] = …` mutates the shared instance every caller uses. Both are fixed by the same change, which is why it is in this phase and not filed as a bug.

## Feature work

### Symbol geometry in the decode result

No reference library returns the symbol's position for Standard QR (CodeGlyphX does it for Micro QR only), so this is a differentiator, and it is cheap: the image decoders already build a `PerspectiveTransform`, and the corners are that transform applied to the four corners of module space.

The contract to settle before writing it (D3): which four points, in which space, in which order, and what a matrix-level decode reports. The intended answer is the outer corners of the module area excluding the quiet zone, in source-image pixel coordinates, ordered from the symbol's own top-left — its own, so the quad also conveys rotation and mirroring — with a matrix-level decode leaving the member at its default and a documented way to tell that apart. The type is a small `readonly struct` pair in the core; `System.Numerics.Vector2` is not used, because on netstandard2.0 it would add a package dependency to a package that advertises none.

### Structured Append (Standard QR only)

rMQR does not define it (recorded in [rmqr-encoder.md](../specs/rmqr-encoder.md)) and neither does Micro QR; both keep reporting `UnsupportedContent`. For Standard QR the work is two-sided:

- **Decode** currently rejects the mode as `UnsupportedContent`. After this phase it reads the header and reports symbol index, total count and parity on `QRCodeDecodeInfo`, returning that symbol's own text. A caller concatenates in index order after checking that the parity bytes agree.
- **Encode** splits content across symbols. The parity byte is the XOR of *the original input bytes*, taken before splitting — not derived from the segment plan, which is where CodeGlyphX diverges from every other encoder. QrCodeGenerator is the correct parity reference since its own bug was fixed in `5c6fdfd`.

Open (D4): whether the encode entry point balances the split automatically across the fewest symbols, or takes an explicit count, and whether a "combine these results" helper ships with it. The minimal surface is one method that returns the symbols plus documented rules for recombination; a helper is easy to add in a minor and impossible to remove.

### Kanji encoding

Today all three symbologies decode Kanji mode and none of them writes it; the scope row in [qrcode-symbologies.md](../specs/qrcode-symbologies.md) says "decode only, revisit on concrete demand". This phase flips that row. Four pieces:

1. **A reverse table**, Unicode → the 13-bit compacted value, generated by `tools/QRInteropFixtures` from the same sweep data that produced `ShiftJisKanjiTable`, so the two cannot disagree. Characters outside the JIS X 0208 repertoire simply have no reverse entry and fall through to Byte mode, which is also what makes the seven-cell CP932 divergence a non-issue for encoding.
2. **A Kanji state in `ModeSegmenter`** (7 states → 8), at a flat 13 bits per character, with per-symbology and per-version availability the way `allowAlnum` / `allowByte` already work: Micro QR M3 and M4 only, all rMQR versions, all Standard QR versions. The per-symbology Kanji count-indicator tables already exist on the decode side.
3. **`EncodingMode` gains Kanji.** The enum deliberately excludes it today ("that enum names the modes the encoder can produce"); this phase is what makes that comment false.
4. **Cross-verification against the external oracles** (qrtool, ZXingCpp, ZXing.Net, libzint) plus committed fixtures, since a Kanji encoder that no third-party reader agrees with is worse than no Kanji encoder.

Two decisions inside the phase. **D5:** whether single-mode selection picks Kanji automatically. It is the cheapest single mode for Japanese text, so saying yes changes the bytes the library emits by default for existing callers — acceptable in a major, and it is what other libraries do, but it must be a decision and a migration note rather than a side effect. **D6:** whether a plan may mix Kanji segments with ECI-tagged Byte segments in one symbol. Legal per the standard, historically uneven across readers; the oracle sweep from piece 4 answers it, and the conservative fallback is to suppress Kanji whenever an ECI header is emitted.

## Open decisions

| # | Decision | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Drop the `string` convenience overloads once the parameter-list overloads are gone? | **Decided 2026-09-06: drop.** All four (`QRCodeGenerator` ×2, `MicroQRCodeGenerator` ×1, `RmQRCodeGenerator` ×1). `string` converts implicitly to `ReadOnlySpan<char>`, so `Create("text", ecc)` keeps compiling and the overloads contribute a parameter name and nothing else. (Corrected during the pre-PR review: this holds on three of the four assets, not all four. See the Phase 1-3 review entry in the Progress log.) `Create` becomes two methods per symbology, span and span-plus-destination, which also removes the asymmetry where only Standard QR had `(string, ecc, destination)` |
| D2 | `SymbolRenderer` / `SymbolImageBuilderBase<TSelf>` as the shared-renderer names | **Decided 2026-09-06: adopt**, together with `QRCodeExtensions` → `SKCanvasExtensions`. "Symbol" is the word both standards and these specs already use for the thing all three symbologies produce; the per-symbology `*ImageDecoder` / `*ImageBuilder` types keep their prefixes |
| D3 | Geometry contract: which corners, which space, which order, matrix-level behaviour | **Decided 2026-09-07.** The outer corners of the module area, quiet zone excluded, as `SymbolCorners` of four `ImagePoint`s (`float X`, `float Y`) in **continuous** image coordinates — (0, 0) is the top-left corner of the top-left pixel, (width, height) the bottom-right corner of the image, so the values plot directly in SkiaSharp / canvas / System.Drawing; the finder centres the decoders anchor on are already in that convention, so nothing is shifted (the review round removed a +0.5 that had been added on the opposite assumption). Ordered from the symbol's own top-left (the finder side): `TopLeft, TopRight, BottomRight, BottomLeft`, so a mirrored capture shows as reversed winding. Populated only when `Status == Success`; matrix-level decodes and failures leave `Corners` at `default`, which `IsEmpty` reports. Both types are library-built `readonly record struct`s (internal constructor, get-only), the Phase 3 rule |
| D4 | Structured Append encode API shape and whether a combine helper ships | Auto-balanced split, no combine helper in 2.0.0 |
| D5 | Does `Segmentation.Single` choose Kanji mode automatically? | Yes, with a migration note; explicit `Utf8Bom` / `EciMode` settings keep Byte mode |
| D6 | Kanji segments mixed with ECI-tagged Byte segments | Let the oracle sweep decide; suppress Kanji under ECI if any oracle disagrees |
| D7 | `EciMode` enum → a value type with `FromValue` / `Value` | **No.** An encoder can only emit a charset it can convert text into (Latin-1 and UTF-8), and the decoder reports every other ECI as `UnsupportedContent` without needing to carry the number. A value type would also need a sentinel for "no ECI", which collides with the real ECI 0, in exchange for expressing values nothing can produce or consume. Recorded as a scope decision with this reason rather than left open |

## Phases

Each phase follows the test-first workflow, regenerates both `PublicAPI.approved.txt` files, updates `docs/migration.md` and the affected specs in the same change, and appends a Progress log entry with Done / Lessons / benchmark delta. A phase that moves a hot path measures it; a phase that only renames states that it did not.

| # | Phase | Contents | Exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Announced removals | The removals table; retire `SizingExceptionContractTest`; default the `options` parameter on all three generators | Surface shrinks, no rename yet |
| 2 | Renames | Both rename tables; the `string` overload removal from D1; internal namespaces and test namespaces follow | One reviewable `PublicAPI.approved.txt` diff |
| 3 | Shape unification | `*CalculatedSize`, `*DecodeInfo` member set, `GradientOptions`, `IconData`, sealing (`Vector2Slim` went with the Phase 2 rename table) | **API-final for the cleanup.** Tag `2.0.0-preview.3` |
| 4 | Symbol geometry | D3, the geometry members on all three `*DecodeInfo`, all three image decode paths | Matrix-level decode behaviour documented and tested |
| 5 | Structured Append | D4, decode-side header reporting, encode-side split, parity over original input bytes | Round-trip plus oracle cross-check |
| 6 | Kanji encoding | D5, D6, reverse table, segmenter state, `EncodingMode`, capacity docs | Oracle sweep green. Tag `2.0.0-preview.4` |
| 7 | Docs and API freeze | `docs/migration.md` 2.0.0 section rewritten with the full rename table and a mechanical replacement script; README, DESIGN.md, spec scope rows (Kanji, Structured Append, geometry); fold this plan into the specs and delete it | Approved API listing frozen |
| 8 | Release | Below | `2.0.0` on nuget.org |

Phases 4-6 are independent of each other and depend only on 1-3. Phase 6 is last so that it can move to 2.1.0 without reopening anything.

## Release checklist (Phase 8)

- `tools/QRInteropFixtures` manual spot-checks, including new ones for Kanji-mode and Structured Append symbols
- Physical scanner acceptance pass, weighted toward Kanji-mode and Structured Append symbols, which are the two outputs no committed fixture can prove a phone accepts
- `PackageValidationBaselineVersion` set to `2.0.0` in both packed projects — the csproj comments already say "no baseline until 2.0.0 ships; set it then"
- `SkiaSharp.QrCode` 2.0.0 stays an empty metapackage; `tools/check_package_deps.cs` asserts the graph after pack, as it does today
- Version bump: `tools/bump_version.cs` parses only `X.Y.Z`, so going from `2.0.0-preview.4` to `2.0.0` is a hand edit of `Directory.Build.props` and the README install lines, or the tool learns prerelease first. Decide which inside the phase; the tool already prints the manual instruction. **It also does not currently compile** — `error CS0106` on a `static readonly` field declared among top-level statements, broken since the core split and unnoticed because nothing in CI runs it. The preview bumps in this line were done by hand. Fixing or deleting it is its own change, not part of the API work
- GitHub release notes lead with the migration table link; the Playground redeploys from the same tag

## Progress log

Entries are appended per phase: what was done, what was learned, and the benchmark delta or an explicit statement that no hot path moved.

### Phase 1, announced removals (2026-09-06)

**Done.** `Compression`, both throwing `GetRequiredBufferSize` methods and all seven parameter list `Create*` overloads are gone; the ten surviving `Create*` entry points and `TryGetRequiredBufferSize` all take `in {Sym}CodeGeneratorOptions options = default`, so `CreateQrCode(text, ecc)` still compiles and now resolves to the options path. Core drops from 34 exported types to 33, `QRCodeGenerator` from 10 public methods to 5, `MicroQRCodeGenerator` from 8 to 4; both `PublicAPI.approved.txt` files regenerated, and the renderer listing is unchanged. 119 call sites migrated across tests, benchmarks, Playground, samples and `tools/QRInteropFixtures`. `docs/migration.md` gains an "announced removals" section with the argument-to-property table and the `-1` trap; the spec's API-direction paragraphs move to past tense and its exception-disagreement record becomes a lesson. Full suite green: 17,609 tests, 0 failures, both target frameworks.

**Lessons.** Recorded in [qrcode-symbologies.md](../specs/qrcode-symbologies.md): differential tests die with their reference and had to be converted to frozen values *before* the deletion; `required` members make the implicit constructor `[Obsolete]`, which read as an announced removal in the approved listing and is not one (`IconData()` was on this plan's removal list in error); and the one break the compiler could not find, `requestedVersion: -1` against a `QRCodeVersionRange` that rejects `-1` on purpose.

**Benchmarks: not run, no hot path moved.** The removed overloads were forwarding wrappers; the surviving options path and the private `Create*Core` methods are byte-identical. The only benchmark files touched are decode-fixture builders (`BuildModules` and friends), outside any measured method.

**Playground verified by hand**, since `QrInterop` changed: published Debug WASM, served it, and encoded through all four paths the change touches — Standard QR automatic (v5), Standard QR pinned (v10, 65×65), Micro QR automatic (M2, 17×17) and Micro QR pinned (M4, 21×21). Decode was not re-checked; no decode call site changed.

**Not done here, by design.** `QRCodeCalculatedSize`'s public constructor and `IsValid` are listed under the removals table but belong to Phase 3's value-kind unification, and D1 (the `string` convenience overloads) stays with Phase 2 where the rest of the shape decisions are.

### Phase 2, renames (2026-09-06)

**Done.** Both rename tables applied, plus D1: the four `string` convenience overloads are gone, so every generator is two `Create` methods (span, span-plus-destination) and `TryGetRequiredBufferSize`. `Vector2Slim` is internal and moved under `FeatherQR.SkiaSharp.Internals`; the `Internals/RmQr` folder is `Internals/RmQR`, matching its namespace and its `MicroQR` / `StandardQR` siblings. Core stays at 33 exported types, the rendering package drops to 25 (`Vector2Slim`), 58 across both. 216 files touched; full suite green (17,609 tests, both target frameworks), and the golden-pixel tests passing is what proves the mechanical rewrite changed names and nothing else. Playground re-verified in WASM (QR v5 automatic, QR pinned v10, Micro QR M2, rMQR R9x139) and its committed API page regenerated. `docs/migration.md` gains the rename table and a runnable replacement script; the naming rule itself is now recorded in [qrcode-symbologies.md](../specs/qrcode-symbologies.md) under "Public API direction", since this plan is deleted at the end.

**Test names followed the API.** `CreateQrCode_*` / `CreateMicroQRCode_*` test methods became `Create_*`, `QRCodeRendererRunMergeParityTest` became `SymbolRendererRunMergeParityTest`, and `QRCodeSegmentationTest` became `QRSegmentationTest`. Benchmark class names were left alone on purpose: they are the identity of historical BenchmarkDotNet reports, and `QRCodeSegmentationEncode` reads as English rather than as a type reference.

**Lessons.** Two are worth carrying (both recorded in the spec): PowerShell's `-ne` is case-insensitive, so a case-only rename silently writes nothing; and a blanket identifier rewrite reaches third-party API with the same spelling — `QRCoder.QRCodeGenerator.ECCLevel` in the comparator benchmarks was renamed along with ours and only the compiler caught it. A third is process rather than code: `@(@('a','b'))` collapses to a two-element array in PowerShell, so `$pair[0]` became a *character* and `String.Replace(char, char)` corrupted three test files. They were restored from HEAD (Phase 1 was committed) and the rules re-applied; the lesson is to build replacement pairs as `[pscustomobject]` or ordered dictionaries, never as nested arrays.

**Benchmarks: not run, no hot path moved.** Renames only; the two call sites that changed shape (`string` overload callers) now bind to the span overload the string one forwarded to.

### Phase 3, shape unification (2026-09-06)

**Done.** `QRCodeCalculatedSize` is a non-positional `readonly record struct` with an internal constructor and get-only properties, like its two siblings: the public constructor, `IsValid`, the `init` setters and deconstruction are gone, while `ToString()`, `==` and `IEquatable<T>` stay (the first cut removed those too; see the rework note below). `GradientOptions` is a `sealed record class` that copies the arrays it is given, reads them back as `ReadOnlySpan<T>` (`ColorPositions` empty rather than null when evenly distributed) and compares by element — the generated equality it replaces compared arrays by reference, so identical gradients were unequal and `Default` was publicly mutable. `IconData` is `sealed` with `init`-only properties. `QRCodeData`, `MicroQRCodeData`, `RmQRCodeData` and the three image builders are `sealed`. `TypeShapeTest` (36 cases) is the new guard for all of it. Full suite green: 17,659 tests, both target frameworks. **This is the API-final point for the cleanup; `2.0.0-preview.3` can be tagged from here.**

**One item of the plan turned out to be already true.** The `*DecodeInfo` member order was listed as inconsistent, and it is not: all three declare `Status, Version, EccLevel, [MaskPattern,] ErrorsCorrected` in that order, with matching constructor order. What differs is the *approved API listing*, which sorts members by type and name, and reading the listing rather than the source is what produced the claim. The test now pins the member set instead, which is the property that actually matters.

**Second round of rework, from an adversarial review (2026-09-06).** Three reviewers and three refutation passes found the same mistake still in place elsewhere: demoting the six result values to plain structs had also removed `ToString` (a logged size printed as the type name), `==` and `IEquatable<T>` — measured 64 bytes of boxing per `Equals` — while `ModuleRect` and the three generator options next door stayed `readonly record struct`. `IconData` had lost `with` the same way `GradientOptions` had. Both are now `record`s again with the members that were actually wrong (public constructor, `init` setters on results) still removed, so the public surface gains only `IEquatable<T>` on seven types and loses nothing. The rule that came out of it is in the spec: name the member that is wrong and remove *that*, rather than reaching for the enclosing kind. **`with` is offered for the members that carry no invariant, and that line is now written down.** `GradientOptions.Direction` is `init`; `Colors` and `ColorPositions` are not, because `with` assigns one member at a time and those two have to agree in length — an `init` colour list would let a caller build a gradient whose stops no longer match and find out only when it is drawn. Verified that a span property *can* take an `init` accessor, and that doing so lets exactly that mismatch through, which is what settled it. `IconData` needs no carve-out because none of its members validate against another at construction, which is why the two option types differ. A `WithColors` wither was written to carry the direction and stops for the caller, and then dropped: it saved two copied-over arguments and nothing else — a mismatched colour count throws either way — and nothing in the repository recolours an existing gradient, so it was API added on anticipation. The reason sits in a code comment where the methods were.

**The migration guide was the symptom, not the defect.** The recolour recipe had to read `options.ColorPositions.IsEmpty ? null : options.ColorPositions.ToArray()` because `GradientOptions` handed colours back as spans and took them as arrays, and spelled "no stops" as empty on the way out and `null` on the way in. The constructor takes spans now, empty on both sides, so the line is `new GradientOptions([…], options.Direction, options.ColorPositions)`. Arrays still convert implicitly, so no existing call site changed; what changed is that `null` is no longer passable for the stops and an empty array now means "evenly distributed" instead of throwing. Documenting an unreadable incantation would have shipped the asymmetry.

Four more findings from the same round were fixed with it: the migration guide's recolour recipe silently dropped `ColorPositions` (it now carries them, and says why the omission is invisible); `README.md` still described `GetRequiredBufferSize` as deprecated-but-present, a release out of date; `ShapeHierarchies_StayOpen_AndTheBuilderBaseDoesNot` ran `All()` over the *non-public* constructors, which a public constructor empties, so it passed vacuously for the violation it names — it now asserts the public constructor list is empty, demonstrated by making the constructor public and watching the test fail; and the immutability wording claimed the colour array was unreachable, which `MemoryMarshal.GetReference` disproves with no `unsafe` and no opt-in, so the documented guarantee is "immutable through the API". Naming the escape hatch in the XML remarks was the first attempt and was wrong for the same reason a library does not caveat reflection: it is noise in front of a caller who wants a gradient, and it is not a threat anyone can close. What the finding was really about is the *absolute* claim, which a later change could have leaned on to skip the defensive copy; the qualifier alone carries that, and the reasoning sits in a code comment beside the property. The last finding, that `GradientOptions` is no longer System.Text.Json-serializable, was closed as accepted: through 1.x it serialized only incidentally and emitted `SKColor`'s `{Alpha,Red,Green,Blue}` shape, which no caller wants persisted, and the Playground — the only JSON consumer here — already maps to its own DTO of `#RRGGBB` strings. A `JsonConverter` would put a System.Text.Json dependency on the netstandard builds and change the packed dependency graph, which is not worth paying before someone asks with a use case. The reasoning is a code comment beside the property, at the maintainer's request; it is deliberately not in the XML docs or the migration guide.

**One round of rework, from a maintainer review.** The first cut made `GradientOptions` a plain `sealed class`, which silently removed `with` — an idiom the three generator options structs still support and the README teaches. Restoring the record while keeping the arrays private is what the defect actually called for: the bug was the *public array*, not the record, and a private array makes the record's shallow copy safe rather than dangerous. `Direction` is the only `init` member, so `with { Direction = … }` compiles and `with { Colors = … }` does not, which is the honest split — colours define the gradient, direction is the cheap variation. `PrintMembers` is hand-written because the generated one would print a `ReadOnlySpan<T>` member as a type name and has to compile on four target frameworks.

**Left alone deliberately.** `ModuleRect` keeps its public constructor and `init` members: it is a geometry value a caller may also build (for tests or their own layout), not an answer the library hands back, so the `Try`-result rule does not apply to it. The generator options structs keep `init` for the same reason in reverse — a caller builds those.

**Benchmarks: not run, no hot path moved.** The only behavioural change is `GradientOptions` copying two small arrays once at construction, outside any measured path; the renderer reaches the same arrays through an internal property. The Playground was not re-verified because `QrInterop` did not change in this phase, and the gradient rendering path is covered by the committed golden PNGs in `RenderingApprovalTest`.

### Phases 1-3 pre-PR adversarial review (2026-09-07)

**Done.** Five parallel reviewers over the whole `main...api_break` diff, then three-verifier refutation rounds on the claims that carried a design consequence. Fixes, in severity order.

**The branch did not compile in Release.** `QRCodeDecoderRoundTripTest.cs:150` sat inside `#if !DEBUG` and still called the removed parameter list overload, so `dotnet build -c Release` — the first step of CI — failed. Debug builds clean, which is why the "full suite green, both target frameworks" claim in the Phase 1-3 entries above was Debug-only, and why `Decode_CharSpanDestination_IsAllocationFree`, the sole zero-allocation guard on the span decode path, had never executed on this branch. It runs and passes now.

**The `string` overload removal rested on a false premise, and took the option structs down with it.** D1 recorded that `string` converts implicitly to `ReadOnlySpan<char>` on all four target frameworks. It converts on three. The conversion is compiler-synthesized rather than an operator on `System.String`, and when `ReadOnlySpan<T>` comes from the `System.Memory` package instead of the framework — the netstandard2.0 asset, which is what .NET Framework 4.6.2+ binds — only C# 14 synthesizes it; every version through 13 reports `CS1503`. Measured against a consumer project, not inferred: the same consumer compiles and *runs* against the published `SkiaSharp.QrCode` 1.2.0 and against a pack of `main`, and fails against this branch. The larger half was underneath it. `init` accessors need C# 9, so on netstandard2.0 (default C# 7.3) and netstandard2.1 (default C# 8.0) the option structs became unconfigurable the moment Phase 1 removed the parameter lists — `with`, a constructor, property assignment and implicit conversion all refused, leaving `Create(text.AsSpan(), ecc)` with defaults and nothing else. All three option structs, and `IconData`, now carry a constructor that assigns through the same `init` accessors, so equality is unchanged and validation is identical on the three option structs; `IconData` deliberately differs in one place, its constructor rejecting a null `Icon` because that route is reached from compilers with no nullable analysis. `IconData` was the same defect found one round later and is the sharper case: its only other public routes are two factories that both hardcode `ImageIconShape`, so `ImageTextIconShape` and any caller-written `IconShape` — the documented extension point, and the spelling the README teaches — were unreachable below C# 9. `TypeShapeTest` states the rule rather than the instance: every settable option has a constructor parameter of the same type, and only a `required` member may be mandatory, because an option reachable only through an object initializer is unreachable below C# 9.

**Lessons.** Four, all recorded in [qrcode-symbologies.md](../specs/qrcode-symbologies.md) so they survive this plan being deleted. A claim about *consumer* compilation cannot be checked from the library's own build, which compiles at C# 14 and therefore proves nothing; it needs a consumer project at the SDK-default language version, and preferably one that also runs. A blanket rename sweep reaches the repository's own released package, not just third-party API: `samples/Dotfiles/FinderPatternAlwaysBlack.cs` pins `SkiaSharp.QrCode@1.0.0` and had its calls rewritten to 2.0.0 names, the same trap the Phase 2 lesson records for QRCoder, one directory over. And a differential test whose reference is deleted becomes a tautology rather than a failure: `ArgumentErrorPrecedenceTest.OptionsAndParameterList_ReportTheSameArgumentError` survived the sweep comparing a call to a textually identical copy of itself, which the Phase 1 lesson predicted for the three test classes it converted to frozen values but did not catch here.

A fourth is the Phase 2 case-only-rename lesson, widened. Phase 2 stranded one prose mention of `Internals/RmQr`, but the sweep for it also uncovered twenty-nine spec-map links pointing at `Internals/StandardQr/` that had been stale since well before this branch — that folder was already `StandardQR` on `main`. Each is a 404 on GitHub and on any case-sensitive checkout, and a link checker run on Windows reports them all as fine because the filesystem is case-insensitive. Resolving each link against `git ls-files` rather than against the disk is what found them; a case-only rename needs a case-sensitive oracle, and on this machine the index is the only one available.

**Also fixed.** Six `<paramref name="data"/>` tags naming a parameter called `bitmap`, which shipped 24 `CS1734` warnings into the published XML docs; `GradientOptions.Equals` could regress to comparing stop *counts* with every gradient test still green, so the missing equivalence classes are now asserted (proven by mutation); the Standard QR `ArgumentException` for an undefined ECC level and Micro QR's quiet zone upper bound, both of which lost their only test with `SizingExceptionContractTest`; `TypeWithNoExtensionPoint_IsSealed` was a hand-maintained list of eight types rather than a rule, and now sweeps both assemblies against a declared set of four extension points; three benchmarks that became exact duplicates when the overloads they were paired against were removed; all six `samples/Dotfiles` entries, which had been left half-migrated (`Sample.cs` gets its namespaces and project reference like the rest, but is a directives-only template with no body, so it still does not build, exactly as on `main`); and stale prose across `standardqr-encoder.md`, `rmqr-encoder.md`, all three spec maps, `README.md` and `docs/migration.md`, including a dead link, two spec-map rows pointing into the wrong package, and two test method names the `\b`-anchored sweep could not match. The committed Playground API page was regenerated too. It was three commits stale, so it advertised none of the new constructors, and since Phase 2 it had carried 347 SourceLink URLs pinned to an unmerged commit — which `release.yaml` and the Playground README both say the committed copy must not have, `--source-links` belonging to the release job alone because that one builds at the tag. `main` carries none; the page carries none again.

**Benchmarks: not run, no hot path moved.** The option struct constructors are additive and execute only where a caller builds an option set; the `GradientOptions.PrintMembers` change removes a boxing conversion on a diagnostic path. An ad-hoc differential sweep run during the review (31,296 encode/decode and 1,728 rendering cases, against a build of `main`; not a committed artifact) produced zero differences, so the "renames only" claim of Phases 1-3 is now measured rather than asserted.

### Phase 4, symbol geometry (2026-09-07)

**Done.** D3 decided and recorded above. Two shared, library-built record structs in the core, `ImagePoint` (`float X`, `float Y`) and `SymbolCorners` (`TopLeft`, `TopRight`, `BottomRight`, `BottomLeft`, `IsEmpty`); a `Corners` member on all three `*DecodeInfo` types, attached through an internal `WithCorners` so the matrix decoders stay ignorant of geometry; one internal helper, `SymbolGeometry`, that projects the four grid corners through whichever mapping the decoder sampled with (a `PerspectiveTransform`, or Micro QR's affine `origin + u·col + v·row` frame, or the mesh-anchored transform Standard QR builds when the piecewise mesh sampled). Standard QR and Micro QR carry one extra bit out of their mirror retry (whether the transposed matrix was the one that decoded) and swap `TopRight`/`BottomLeft` on it; rMQR's frames already swap axes, so its transform is in symbol order. Core goes from 33 to 35 exported types; the rendering package is unchanged. `SymbolCornersTest` (axis-aligned to a tenth of a pixel, 90°/180°/270° and oblique rotation, mirror with reversed winding, keystone per version, matrix decode and the three failure classes empty, luminance and bitmap overloads agree) and the `TypeShapeTest` additions; full suite green at 17,813 tests across both target frameworks (17,831 in Release). README, `docs/migration.md` (additive section), the shared contract in [qrcode-symbologies.md](../specs/qrcode-symbologies.md) and the per-symbology notes in the Standard QR and rMQR decoder records are updated; the Playground is untouched (showing the outline there is a follow-up, not part of this phase).

**Accuracy, as first measured (superseded by the review round below).** Half a module for flat, rotated and mirrored captures on all three symbologies; under keystone, Standard QR with an alignment pattern holds half a module, Micro QR and rMQR one module. Two of those statements did not survive adversarial review: the keystone cases had only exercised versions below the mesh threshold (the mesh needs version 14 and up, not 7), and the Micro QR and rMQR rotation/keystone bounds were measured at a single lucky angle and a single lenient tilt.

**Review round (2026-09-07).** Five reviewer lenses in parallel, then three refutation agents per surviving claim; six claims reached the shortlist, none was refuted by two of three, so all six were fixed against a red test or a measured assertion.
- *Mesh path reported an unvalidated transform.* When the piecewise mesh sampled (version 14+), `Corners` came from the global 4-point transform the decode never validated: 18 to 30 modules off at the bottom-right on a keystoned version 16. Fixed by `MeshAnchoredTransform`, a quad fit through the three finder centres and the mesh's bottom-right lattice node; bilinear extrapolation of the outer mesh cell was tried first and left the top-left 0.6 to 0.75 module short. Keystone tests at that pass covered versions 2, 7, 20, 25 and 30 at half a module (2, 5, 7, 10, 14, 20, 25 and 30 after the later passes).
- *A half-pixel shift that was a bias.* `SymbolGeometry` added 0.5 px on the theory that the decoders sample in an "integer = pixel centre" convention; the finder centres are edge-convention already (exclusive run ends), so every finder-anchored corner sat half a pixel outside the symbol. Removed; a tenth-of-a-pixel axis-aligned test pins it. Alignment-anchored (`AlignmentPatternFinder` refines Y with `+0.5f`) and sub-finder-anchored (rMQR dark-run centre, about −0.75) corners keep sub-pixel residuals of their own; unifying those anchor conventions is a follow-up, not a corner bug.
- *Micro QR oblique rotation is not half a module.* The finder-axis sweep scores integer-pixel runs, flat for ±3–4° around the truth, and the first 1° candidate that decodes wins; corners 13 to 19 modules from the finder move 0.2 to 0.9 module at 8, 16 and 32 px per module alike. Contract relaxed to about a module for oblique Micro QR; tests at 8°, 20°, 60°, 75° and a rotated mirror hold that.
- *rMQR keystone exceeds a module on short symbols.* One of the two far corners, 1.22 to 1.24 modules at 3 to 4 % on R11x59 (the shear search under-recovers the column-axis lean and the first decoding transform wins; the figures first quoted, 1.27 to 1.30, were taken with the half-pixel shift still in). Contract says a module and a half from 3 % up on short symbols; tests cover R7x43, R11x59 and R17x139 at 4 %, and the spec record no longer names one corner as the worst (it is the bottom-left on R11x59 at 3 to 4 % and the top-right on R7x43, so neither "top-right" as first written nor "bottom-left" as corrected).
- *Negative tests were too weak.* A mutant that attached corners on every terminal status passed the whole suite: the only negative test used a blank image, which exits as `NotDetected` before any attach site. Added `DestinationTooSmall` (one-char destination) and `DataUncorrectable` (a painted-over data block) on all three symbologies, asserting `Corners.IsEmpty`.
- *Docs said what the code should do, not what it does.* Accuracy text in `SymbolCorners`, the shared contract, the rMQR and Standard QR decoder records and the migration guide now state the measured envelope, and the "integer = pixel centre" sentence is gone.
A second reviewer pass on the docs then caught the contract quoting the *tested* keystone range as the decoder's envelope and three copies of the same measurement with three different numbers; the keystone tests now run at 12 % on versions 2 and 5, 6 to 8 % on 7 and 10, 5 to 6 % from 14 up, and Micro QR at 2, 4, 5 and 8 % (most versions decode further on that scene and hold the bound there too), and every figure has one source. A third pass found the rMQR figures had been measured before the half-pixel shift was removed; they are re-measured from the shipped code.

**Branch-wide review round (2026-09-09).** Four reviewer lenses over the whole branch, then three refutation agents per shortlisted claim; five claims survived at 3/3, one ("the corner tolerances are one rasterizer rounding from red") was dropped at 2/3 refuted, and the merge from `main` was independently verified to have lost nothing. What it found, in the order it matters.
- *The Playground drew the outline in the wrong place for EXIF-rotated photos.* `imageOrientation: 'none'` does not suppress EXIF — it is a legacy alias for `from-image`, and `flipY` applies the tag too, so no option value opts out. Skia decodes the stored pixels, the browser displays the oriented ones, and the width/height guard only catches the tags that swap dimensions: for tags 2, 3 and 4 the outline landed on blank paper under a confident caption, and a mirrored photo was reported "not mirrored". Fixed by reading the tag with `SKCodec.EncodedOrigin` (which Skia parses and then ignores) and mapping the corners through it, so all eight orientations now draw correctly and the winding describes what the viewer sees; measured at 2 px of the symbol on every tag.
- *Two overlapping decodes crossed their results.* Pasting twice, or dropping during a decode, left the canvas showing the first image while the result line described the second, and leaked the loser's `ImageBitmap`. Reproduced at a 20 ms gap with no artificial delay, because a small image resolves faster than a large one. Fixed with a generation token that also closes the bitmap the superseded run made.
- *The half-module accuracy figure was true only at 8 px per module and up.* The bottom-right corner is anchored on the alignment pattern, whose centre resolves to about a pixel at any module size, so its error is near-constant in pixels (4.09 px at 6 px per module, 3.63 at 8, 3.94 at 12) and the module figure grows as the capture coarsens — 0.68 module at 6, and 0.58 on a *flat, axis-aligned* version 2 at 2 px per module, where version 1 measures exactly zero because it is finder-anchored. No minimum density was documented anywhere, and `FinderPatternFinder` calls 3 px per module the bottom of the envelope. The contract now states the density, and four rows pin the pixel bound.
- *Any version can silently get version 1's looser fit.* When the bottom-right alignment pattern is not found, `BuildGridTransform` falls back to the finders-only parallelogram on every version, error correction still returns `Success`, and one erased module is enough to trigger it (v2 at 3 % keystone: 1.00 module out; v10 at 1 %: 1.11). The contract named version 1 as the only loose case; it now names both, and three rows assert the fallback is genuinely in use rather than only that the corner is within bounds.
- *A third mirrored attach site was unexercised.* Micro QR's arbitrary-orientation sweep, mirrored branch: dropping its `transposed` flag swapped TopRight with BottomLeft by about 24 modules and reversed the winding, and the whole suite stayed green. An 8° row closes the last empty cell in the mapping × mirror table.
- Also fixed: a page-wide paste stole clipboards that carry a bitmap *alongside* text (Excel, Word), and then, after the first fix, stole nothing at all when focus sat on a checkbox; a synchronous WASM decode froze the page for up to 4.3 s with no busy state, and the first attempt at one did not paint because a single `requestAnimationFrame` resolves before the frame it schedules; a preview failure un-hid the figure still holding the previous image and its outline. The sample now exits non-zero when a scene stops decoding, guards its canvas bounds, and states its keystone arithmetic correctly.

**A fix that was reverted rather than kept.** The mesh corner anchor was changed to the bottom-right-most *detected* lattice node, because the comment claimed the anchor was a node the decode had validated and that was not guaranteed. Measured against the unchanged code on every mesh version and tilt, with the diagonal pattern erased included, the two produce byte-identical corners — the mesh's refinement rounds have already re-predicted that node from a homography through the nodes it did find. Unobservable code that no test can pin is worse than an honest comment, so the plumbing came out and the comment now says what the anchor actually is. The reviewer's related point stands on its own: a claim in a comment is a claim, and this one had to be either made true or withdrawn. `SymbolCornersTest` is 62 cases after the round (the third pass added a mirrored keystone on the version-20 mesh path and Micro QR keystones at 5 and 8 % plus a mirrored 8 %, which are the only rows that reach the mesh's and the single-finder perspective search's attach sites; a mutant dropping the transposed flag at either site had passed the suite).

**Lessons.** Three, recorded in the spec's contract paragraph and the decoder records. An accuracy figure measured at one angle and one tilt is not a bound: the first draft's "half a module" for Micro QR was true at 20° and false at 8°, 17° and 60°, and rMQR's "one module" was true at 2 % and false at 3 %; sweep the parameter before writing the number. A decoder's internal coordinate convention has to be read off the code that produces the anchors, not inferred from the code that consumes them (the `(int)(x + 0.5f)` samplers looked like a pixel-centre convention and were a rounding). And a negative test has to reach the site it guards: a blank image exits at detection, so it never tested the `Success` gate at all, and a mutant that attached corners on every terminal status passed the whole suite. Follow-ups: a sub-degree refit of the winning single-finder frame after decode (would tighten Micro QR and rMQR to Standard QR's bound), and the alignment/sub-finder anchor convention.

**Benchmarks: no regression; and a lesson about measuring.** The first before/after pair was taken while builds and the test suite ran concurrently, and the matrix-path rows moved +30 to +50 % — impossible for a change that touches the matrix path only by widening an `out` struct from 20 to 52 bytes. Re-measured with the sources stashed to HEAD and the machine idle (ShortRun, both classes back to back): Standard QR matrix rows +0.8 % / +1.0 % / +5.3 % / +1.7 % / +1.2 %, image row −1.1 %, span rows −0.6 % / −0.7 % / +1.0 % / −2.9 % / −3.3 %; rMQR rows −2.9 % to −8.6 %, one +2.2 % with a 7 µs error bar; allocations identical on every row. One row crossed the gate: `QR_Byte_V40_H (Span)` +12.1 % in the clean run. Its string twin, which does strictly more work, moved +1.2 % in the same run, and an immediate re-run of the two V40_H rows put both at +15–19 % over the same baseline, moving together: the 100 µs, RS-heavy version-40 cases drift by that much between ShortRun launches on this machine, and nothing in the change can produce it there. Recorded as noise with that evidence; a MediumRun on those two rows is the next step if certainty is wanted. After the review round (mesh-anchored transform, shift removed) the same two classes were re-run on an idle machine against that clean pre-review run: every Standard QR row −3 to −11 % (image row 33.3 → 31.0 µs, V40_H span 112 → 99 µs, both twins moving together), every rMQR row −2 to −9 %, allocations identical on all rows; nothing crossed the +10 % gate.

**Shown, not just described (2026-09-08).** The corners were listed as a follow-up and then done, because a geometry feature nobody can see is a feature nobody checks. `samples/Dotfiles/DecodeCorners.cs` decodes a flat, a rotated, a mirrored and a keystoned capture of the same symbol and writes each one with the reported outline, the `TopLeft` marker and the four labels drawn on it, so the symbol-frame naming and the reversed winding are visible side by side; the migration guide and the README point at it. The Playground's decode panel, which showed only a line of text, now draws the image on a canvas with the same outline over it and says which way the winding runs. It also takes an image pasted anywhere on the page or dropped on the panel, and a checkbox turns the overlay off for anyone who just wants to read the code. Four details that had to be right. The page maps the corners through the file's EXIF orientation before drawing, because the library decodes the stored pixels and a browser displays the oriented ones; the payload carries both the tag (read with `SKCodec.EncodedOrigin`) and the decoded size, so a residual mismatch drops the overlay instead of drawing it in the wrong place. The canvas is sized in CSS pixels and scaled by the device pixel ratio, with the corners mapped into that space: drawing at the image's own resolution and letting CSS resize the canvas is what made the first version's outline look soft, since a small symbol was being stretched by the browser. Paste is page-wide but skips a target that takes typed text, because a clipboard from Excel or Word carries a bitmap alongside the text and claiming it would lose the user's paste; drop is scoped to the panel, since the logo field takes dropped images too and a page-wide target would swallow those. Verified in a published WASM build: all four captures, a Micro QR pasted from the clipboard, a mirrored capture dropped on the panel, the toggle both ways, a text paste into the content field (not intercepted), a non-image drop, and an image with no code in it (preview shown, honest caption, no stale outline). One thing the sample found on the way: the `SKPath` recipe the migration guide gave for drawing the quadrilateral is obsolete under the SkiaSharp 4.148 the library pins, so both it and the sample use `SKPathBuilder`.

**Left for later, by design.** A derived `IsMirrored` was not added because the winding already carries it and the public-API rule wants a request first. `ImagePoint` keeps its internal constructor and gains no `Deconstruct`, unlike the positional `ModuleRect`, for the same rule: nothing in the API accepts one, so the only gain would be `var (x, y) =` over `.X` / `.Y`, and both are additive later.

### Styling stops at the finder patterns (2026-09-10)

**Found from the Playground.** A Micro QR at module size 92 % rendered fine and decoded as nothing. The first guess, that the Micro QR detector was weaker than the Standard QR one, was wrong twice over: Standard QR fails identically at 92 % when no finder shape is set (the Playground hides it by defaulting to one), and 98 % already fails, so this was a cliff rather than a styling trade-off.

**Diagnosis.** The module shape and size were being applied to the finder patterns. A data module is read by sampling the centre of its cell, so a gap around it costs nothing; a finder is read by scanning for the 1:1:3:1:1 run of dark and light, and a gap splits its three-module dark centre into three runs, after which the ratio exists nowhere in the image and the symbol is never located. At 24 px per module, 92 % means a 1.9 px sliver of white, which is plenty. ZXing fails on the same renders, which is what settled the direction: the output was non-conformant, so the decoder was the wrong place to fix it.

**Scope, measured rather than assumed.** Pasting the 100 % finder back over an otherwise styled render restores every failing case (Micro QR square 92 %, Micro QR circle at 100 % and 85 %, rMQR circle 100 %, Standard QR square 92 %), so the finder is the whole defect. Alignment patterns need nothing: they are found from a predicted position by their single dark centre module, and 75 % modules still decode at versions 2 through 40. All four built-in finder shapes stay detectable with circle data modules down to 75 %, because what matters is that the rings are continuous, not that they are square.

**Done.** `WithModuleShape` styles data modules only. The finder patterns are drawn by a `FinderPatternShape`, defaulting to the plain square, and `WithFinderPatternShape` moved from `QRCodeImageBuilder` to `SymbolImageBuilderBase` so every symbology has it; the Micro QR and rMQR `SymbolRenderer.Render` overloads gained the matching optional parameter, and the two matrix views now report where their finder is instead of returning `false`. Public surface is unchanged in type count. `StyledSymbolDecodabilityTest` (28 cases: three symbologies × shape × size, decorative finders, and the alignment-pattern tolerance that documents why they are *not* protected) went from 18 red to green. Four rendering goldens were regenerated: those are the visual change, a solid finder inside otherwise styled output.

**Lessons.** Two worth carrying. A styling knob that reaches a function pattern is not a trade-off but a cliff, because function patterns are read as shapes and data modules are read as samples — the two are not the same kind of pixel and must not share a control. And when output is rejected by an independent decoder as well as our own, the bug is in the writer: reaching for decoder tolerance would have cost the hottest loop in decoding (finder candidates are 90 % of `FindCandidates`) to rescue symbols we should not have been emitting.

**Benchmarks: fast path flat, styled path faster.** The existing image benchmark only covered full-size squares, which this change leaves byte-identical, so two styled cases were added first. Clean before/after with only the renderer stashed, machine idle: `Small_512px` +0.8 %, `Small_2048px` +0.1 %, `Large_512px` −0.4 %, `Large_2048px` +0.6 % (all inside the noise this class shows, as expected for an untouched path), and the styled rows `Large_512px_Styled` 24.36 → 23.51 ms (−3.5 %) and `Small_512px_Styled` 6.06 → 5.90 ms (−2.7 %). Allocations identical on every row. The win is where the reasoning said it would be: three rectangles per finder instead of thirty-three per-module draws.

**Left for later.** The Playground could expose the finder shape for Micro QR and rMQR now that they support it; the default is correct without it, so this is decoration, not a fix.
